---
title: "02 - Check manual tracing on 3D MIP"
author: "Xinyi Chen"
output: html_document
---

# Purpose

This file visually checks whether the manual tracing for
p28_330_HET_009 aligns with the raw image and the MGtoolbox
preprocessed signal.

It overlays the tracing on maximum-intensity projections (MIPs)
of both three-dimensional volumes, showing the full image and
a closer view of the traced region. These plots assess alignment
in the X-Y plane. A coordinate summary reports the image dimensions
and the tracing's X, Y, and Z ranges.

# Steps

1. Libraries
   Load MGtoolbox for image processing and xml2 for reading
   the manual-tracing file.

2. File paths
   Specify the project directory, sample name, raw TIFF,
   MGtoolbox signal file, and manual-tracing file.

3. Create the raw-image MIP
   Read the raw three-dimensional TIFF stack and calculate
   its maximum-intensity projection along the axial direction.

4. Create the MG-probability MIP
   Load the three-dimensional signal saved in Step01 and
   calculate its maximum-intensity projection.

5. Read the manual tracing
   Read the compressed XML tracing file and extract the
   X, Y, and Z coordinates. Keep tracing paths separate
   so that unrelated endpoints are not connected.

6. Plot helpers
   Define functions for displaying MIPs and overlaying
   the tracing paths. Scale image contrast for display
   using the 1st and 99.8th intensity percentiles.
   This display adjustment leaves the stored volumes unchanged.

7. Generate the alignment figure
   Display four panels: the raw-image and MGtoolbox-signal
   MIPs with tracing overlays, each shown at full view and
   zoomed around the traced region.

8. Print the coordinate summary
   Report the sample name, volume dimensions, numbers of
   tracing paths and points, and coordinate ranges to
   support the alignment check.

The setup chunk controls R Markdown output formatting and
is separate from these processing steps.

```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

## 1. Libraries

```{r libraries}
library(MGtoolbox)
library(xml2)
```

## 2. File paths

```{r paths}
find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
  current <- normalizePath(start, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)

  repeat {
    has_readme <- file.exists(file.path(current, "README.md"))
    has_notebooks <- dir.exists(file.path(current, "notebooks"))
    has_data <- dir.exists(file.path(current, "data"))

    if (has_readme && has_notebooks && has_data) {
      return(current)
    }

    parent <- dirname(current)
    if (identical(parent, current)) {
      stop("Open this file from within the repository containing README.md, notebooks/, and data/.")
    }
    current <- parent
  }
}

project_root <- find_project_root()
sample_name <- "p28_330_HET_009"

raw_dir <- file.path(
  project_root, "data", sample_name, "raw"
)

raw_file <- "p28_330_HET_009.tif"

probability_file <- file.path(
  project_root,
  "results", sample_name, "01_mgtoolbox_signal",
  "p28_330_HET_009_mg_probability_3d.rds"
)

trace_file <- file.path(
  project_root,
  "data", sample_name, "manual_tracing",
  "p28_330_HET_009_manual.traces"
)

```

## 3. Create the raw-image MIP

```{r raw-mip}
stack_list <- read_z_stacks(
  dir = raw_dir,
  filename = raw_file
)

image_stack <- stack_list[[raw_file]]
raw_mip <- MIProject_im(image_stack, along = 3)

dim(image_stack)
dim(raw_mip)
```

## 4. Create the MG-probability MIP

```{r probability-mip}
probability_3d <- readRDS(probability_file)
probability_mip <- MIProject_im(probability_3d, along = 3)

dim(probability_3d)
dim(probability_mip)
```

## 5. Read the manual tracing

The `.traces` file is a gzip-compressed XML file. We keep each path separate
so that unrelated path endpoints are never connected to one another.

```{r read-tracing}
trace_xml_text <- paste(
  readLines(gzfile(trace_file), warn = FALSE),
  collapse = "\n"
)

trace_document <- read_xml(trace_xml_text)
trace_path_nodes <- xml_find_all(trace_document, "//path")

trace_paths <- lapply(seq_along(trace_path_nodes), function(i) {
  point_nodes <- xml_find_all(trace_path_nodes[[i]], ".//point")

  data.frame(
    path_id = i,
    point_id = seq_along(point_nodes),
    x = as.numeric(xml_attr(point_nodes, "x")),
    y = as.numeric(xml_attr(point_nodes, "y")),
    z = as.numeric(xml_attr(point_nodes, "z"))
  )
})

trace_points <- do.call(rbind, trace_paths)

cat("Number of tracing paths:", length(trace_paths), "\n")
cat("Number of tracing points:", nrow(trace_points), "\n")
cat("X range:", range(trace_points$x), "\n")
cat("Y range:", range(trace_points$y), "\n")
cat("Z range:", range(trace_points$z), "\n")
```

## 6. Plot helpers

```{r plot-helpers}
plot_mip <- function(mip, title_text, x_limits = NULL, y_limits = NULL) {
  image_height <- nrow(mip)
  image_width <- ncol(mip)

  if (is.null(x_limits)) {
    x_limits <- c(0, image_width - 1)
  }

  if (is.null(y_limits)) {
    y_limits <- c(image_height - 1, 0)
  }

  display_limits <- quantile(
    as.vector(mip),
    probs = c(0.01, 0.998),
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

  displayed <- (mip - display_limits[1]) /
    (display_limits[2] - display_limits[1])
  displayed <- pmin(pmax(displayed, 0), 1)

  # `displayed` is already a 0-1 matrix.  Passing it directly to
  # as.raster() preserves both the true black-white range and its 2D shape.
  gray_raster <- as.raster(displayed)

  plot(
    NA,
    xlim = x_limits,
    ylim = y_limits,
    axes = FALSE,
    xlab = "",
    ylab = "",
    asp = 1,
    main = title_text
  )

  rasterImage(
    gray_raster,
    xleft = 0,
    ybottom = image_height - 1,
    xright = image_width - 1,
    ytop = 0,
    interpolate = FALSE
  )
}

add_manual_tracing <- function(paths, line_color = "red", line_width = 1) {
  for (one_path in paths) {
    if (nrow(one_path) == 1) {
      points(one_path$x, one_path$y, col = line_color, pch = 16, cex = 0.3)
    } else {
      lines(one_path$x, one_path$y, col = line_color, lwd = line_width)
    }
  }
}
```

## 7. Generate the alignment figure

```{r alignment-figure}
margin <- 50

zoom_x <- c(
  max(0, floor(min(trace_points$x)) - margin),
  min(ncol(raw_mip) - 1, ceiling(max(trace_points$x)) + margin)
)

zoom_y <- c(
  min(nrow(raw_mip) - 1, ceiling(max(trace_points$y)) + margin),
  max(0, floor(min(trace_points$y)) - margin)
)

par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1))

plot_mip(raw_mip, "Raw 3D stack MIP + manual tracing")
add_manual_tracing(trace_paths)

plot_mip(probability_mip, "MGtoolbox 3D probability MIP + manual tracing")
add_manual_tracing(trace_paths)

plot_mip(
  raw_mip,
  "Raw MIP + manual tracing: zoom",
  x_limits = zoom_x,
  y_limits = zoom_y
)
add_manual_tracing(trace_paths, line_width = 1.5)

plot_mip(
  probability_mip,
  "MG probability MIP + manual tracing: zoom",
  x_limits = zoom_x,
  y_limits = zoom_y
)
add_manual_tracing(trace_paths, line_width = 1.5)
```

## 8. Print the coordinate summary

```{r print-summary}
alignment_summary <- data.frame(
  sample = sample_name,
  raw_stack_dimensions = paste(dim(image_stack), collapse = " x "),
  mg_probability_dimensions = paste(dim(probability_3d), collapse = " x "),
  number_of_trace_paths = length(trace_paths),
  number_of_trace_points = nrow(trace_points),
  trace_x_range = paste(range(trace_points$x), collapse = " to "),
  trace_y_range = paste(range(trace_points$y), collapse = " to "),
  trace_z_range = paste(range(trace_points$z), collapse = " to ")
)

alignment_summary
```

# Decision before Step 3

Do not proceed to the 3D target or hitting-probability calculation until the
four-panel figure confirms that:

1. the manual tracing overlays the intended cell in the raw MIP;
2. it overlays the same structure in the MG-probability MIP;
3. X and Y are not swapped or mirrored;
4. the traced structure lies inside the expected sample field.
